question: What are we working on for Feature: `<feature name>`? Describe the rough idea, problem, user, workflow, failure mode, or desired behavior, and I will help shape it into clear, complete, testable project intent.
disposition: Answered. Jared said the feature is called `Free Models`; PM should directly integrate and heavily adapt `https://github.com/vava-nessa/free-coding-models`; the hard part is automatically pulling in upstream changes as the maintainer updates providers/settings; all imported free models should appear under one direct provider called `Free Models`; the GUI comments should link to the upstream GitHub repo.

question: For automatic upstream updates, should PM silently auto-enable safe catalog additions/removals after validation, or should imports land in a review/staging queue where Jared can approve the diff before it changes active model routing?
disposition: Answered. Jared chose `Auto Apply`. Planning interpretation: PM should automatically apply validated upstream changes, while still recording import evidence and quarantining changes that fail PM validation, security/storage boundaries, or source-mapping checks instead of silently changing active routing.

question: For the first Free Models version, should PM import only the upstream provider/model catalog and PM-owned metadata, or should it also adapt upstream runtime behavior such as schema normalizers, router scoring, fallback sets, benchmark/probe loops, and update checks?
disposition: Answered. Jared said adapting upstream runtime behavior like schema normalizers, router scoring, fallback sets, probes, and update checks probably makes the most sense, with the explicit caveat that PM must adapt it to PM's system rather than run upstream behavior as-is.

question: Inside the single PM provider `Free Models`, should PM include every upstream active free/free-limited model with eligibility badges, or filter the default list to stricter no-cost/no-credit-card/no-trial-credit models and expose the rest behind an optional view?
disposition: Answered. Jared chose `every active free/free-limited with badges`. PM should show the broad active free/free-limited set while preserving badges/caveats for setup, quota, rate limits, account requirements, and eligibility confidence.

question: Should the user-defined top-10 Free Models priority list be global for all PM use, or should PM allow separate top-10 lists per role/surface such as general chat, worker, frontend/GUI worker, auditor, or high-effort coding?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `Per role/surface but an option to set it globally. Default to globally to keep the gui cleaner.` Planning interpretation: PM should use a single global top-10 Free Models priority list by default, then expose per-role/surface overrides as an advanced/optional mode so the default GUI remains clean.

question: When Auto Apply removes or marks a user-prioritized Free Models entry unavailable because upstream changed free-tier status, provider support, or model availability, should PM automatically promote the next eligible model and notify, or preserve the disabled top-10 slot until the user edits it?
disposition: Answered. Jared chose `Hybrid`. Planning interpretation: PM should auto-promote the next eligible model for runtime continuity while preserving the invalidated priority entry visibly as disabled/needs-review so the user's preference is not silently erased.

question: Should Free Models auto-switching stay strictly inside the `Free Models` provider after the user or role policy selects it, or may PM also use `Free Models` as a cross-provider fallback when another selected provider/model is exhausted, rate limited, unavailable, or policy-blocked?
disposition: Answered by correction. Jared said `I think top 10 should be across all the providers/models.` Planning interpretation: PM should use a PM-wide top-10 preferred model list across all providers/models, with Free Models entries participating alongside other provider/model entries. This supersedes the narrower idea that top-10 priority is only inside the `Free Models` provider, while preserving the separate catalog requirement that imported free/free-limited models appear under one provider named `Free Models`.

question: For the PM-wide top-10 provider/model list, should costed, paid-overage, or non-free models be eligible whenever their provider is enabled, or should PM require an explicit per-entry opt-in/badge before a model that can spend money or consume paid credits may participate in automatic failover?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `Yes, they should be eligible`. Planning interpretation: paid-overage, metered API, costed, non-free, and credit-consuming models are eligible for PM-wide top-10 automatic failover when their provider/model is enabled; PM should not require a separate per-entry opt-in before automatic routing may use them, while still preserving visible cost/billing/credit badges and Usage evidence.

question: Should PM provide optional budget ceilings or notification thresholds for automatic failover into paid-overage, metered API, costed, or credit-consuming top-10 entries, or should visibility rely only on badges, Usage records, and normal provider/account pressure state?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `Both`. Planning interpretation: PM should provide optional budget ceilings and notification thresholds for automatic failover into costed top-10 entries, while also preserving always-on badges, Usage records, and normal provider/account pressure state.

question: For optional budget ceilings and notification thresholds on costed automatic failover, should the default be warn-only/off until configured, or should PM ship with default notification thresholds such as notify at 50%, 80%, and 100% of a user-set budget?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `do presets and have configurable levels. Default to presets though. 50, 80, 90, 95, 100.` Planning interpretation: PM should ship default budget/notification presets at exactly 50%, 80%, 90%, 95%, and 100% of the configured budget, while allowing the user/team to configure the threshold levels.

question: For Auto Apply upstream updates from `free-coding-models`, should PM check on app launch plus a daily background check by default, or use a different cadence such as manual-only, every few hours, or weekly?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `check on app launch plus a daily background check by default, then be configurable`. Planning interpretation: PM should check upstream on app launch and once daily in the background by default, while allowing the cadence to be configured.

question: When Auto Apply detects and applies upstream changes, should PM show a quiet notification/inbox summary for successful validated imports and reserve blocking review only for quarantined/unsafe changes, or should every applied import produce a more prominent user-facing review item?
disposition: Answered, then superseded by q-0072. Earlier answer chose quiet notification/inbox summaries; Jared later corrected successful Free Models Auto Apply visibility with `1. No notification`, so successful validated updates now create no notification/inbox item.

question: When the manual/all-provider refresh runs, should it refresh catalog/model metadata only by default, or should it also run safe live probes/health/quota checks for providers where that is possible? Probes can spend quota or trigger rate limits, so probe depth should be explicit/configurable.
disposition: Answered. Jared said `the first`. Planning interpretation: manual/all-provider refresh defaults to catalog/model metadata only and does not run live probes, health checks, quota checks, model calls, or quota-spending/rate-limit-triggering checks by default.

question: For Auto Apply, should PM auto-apply only declarative/catalog-safe provider/model changes by default while upstream runtime behavior changes such as schema normalizers, router scoring, fallback sets, probes, and update checks become review/adaptation candidates, or should behavior changes also auto-apply when validation passes?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `Yes auto apply, and Runtime behavior changes should be automatic too, but only for the free model provider.` Planning interpretation: validated upstream runtime behavior changes may auto-apply automatically only for PM's single `Free Models` provider; this does not extend to other direct providers, CLI-backed providers, or PM-wide refresh.

question: For Free Models runtime-behavior Auto Apply, should automatic updates be limited to declarative/parameterized PM behavior descriptors such as normalizer maps, scoring weights, fallback sets, probe definitions, and update-check metadata, while code-level executable adapter changes are quarantined for review, or may PM synthesize/apply code-level behavior adapters automatically after validation?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `You can make it all automatic for the free models. As long as it adapts to the PM structure.` Planning interpretation: Free Models runtime behavior updates may be fully automatic, including deeper synthesized/code-level adapter behavior, but only when adapted into PM structure and validated through PM-owned contracts before activation.

question: If an automatic Free Models catalog or behavior update passes initial validation but later causes runtime failures, degraded routing, bad scoring, or provider breakage, should PM automatically roll back to the previous known-good Free Models provider snapshot and quarantine the update?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `1. Yes`. Planning interpretation: if an automatic Free Models catalog or behavior update later causes runtime failures, degraded routing, bad scoring, or provider breakage, PM should automatically roll back to the previous known-good Free Models provider snapshot and quarantine the update.

question: Should Free Models Auto Apply track the upstream default branch/latest catalog by default because the maintainer changes providers/settings continuously, with pinned-version/rollback controls, or should it only track tagged releases/stable versions?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `2. Yes`. Planning interpretation: Free Models Auto Apply should track the upstream default branch/latest catalog by default, with pinned-version and rollback controls.

question: Should Free Models entries reuse existing PM provider/account credentials and account state when the underlying provider is already configured, showing setup-required badges/actions when credentials are missing, rather than storing separate duplicate Free Models credentials?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `3. Yes`. Planning interpretation: Free Models entries should reuse existing PM provider/account credentials and account state when the underlying provider is already configured, and show setup-required badges/actions when credentials are missing rather than storing duplicate Free Models credentials.

question: When upstream says a Free Models entry is no longer free/free-limited but PM still supports the model through its real provider, should the entry leave the active Free Models list and remain available through the real provider/top-10 route if enabled, while preserving a disabled/history badge in Free Models?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: if a model stops being free/free-limited upstream but remains supported through its real provider, it leaves the active Free Models list, remains available through the real provider/top-10 route if enabled, and keeps disabled/history state in Free Models.

question: If all PM-wide top-10 entries are exhausted, rate limited, unavailable, or policy-blocked, should PM fall back to the best eligible enabled provider/model outside the top 10 with clear switch reason, or stop and ask the user?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `1. Yes`. Planning interpretation: if all PM-wide top-10 entries are exhausted, rate limited, unavailable, or policy-blocked, PM should fall back to the best eligible enabled provider/model outside the top 10 with a clear switch reason instead of stopping.

question: Should the Free Models provider list default to grouping entries by underlying provider with search/filter controls and visible badges for setup, free/free-limited status, quota/pressure, source confidence, and downgrade/history state?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `2. Yes`. Planning interpretation: the Free Models provider list should default to grouping entries by underlying provider with search/filter controls and visible badges for setup, free/free-limited status, quota/pressure, source confidence, and downgrade/history state.

question: After Free Models Auto Apply updates catalog or behavior, should PM run non-consuming structural/contract validation by default and reserve live canary probes/model calls for an explicit configurable verification mode?
disposition: Answered. Jared said `3. Yes`. Planning interpretation: after Free Models Auto Apply updates catalog or behavior, PM should run non-consuming structural/contract validation by default and reserve live canary probes/model calls for an explicit configurable verification mode.

Planning interpretation: PM should not expose a technical Free Models update history/import-diff view as the normal user UI; it should provide plain-language update/status outcomes instead.
